why: PR F of docs/plans/CLOSURE_SEARCH_SCALING_AND_VALIDATION_PLAN_2026-08-10.md requires the decision parameters to be fixed BEFORE the benchmark that judges cost-ordered execution runs, so a disappointing comparison cannot be repaired by moving a threshold afterwards.

inherited_from.note: v3 changes EXECUTION ORDER only. Every decision parameter is copied from v2 unchanged, so a difference in outcome between the two can only come from the execution order — which is exactly the hypothesis the equivalence gate tests. v1 and v2 are untouched.

hypothesis: For the same candidates, costs, policy and hard-failure outcomes, independent-cost-ordered-exact produces the same pilot status and the same selected_ids as independent-exhaustive, while running SUMO on strictly fewer candidates.

requires: a named pre-outcome benchmark with several health-viable candidates
identical candidate costs, hard failures, finalist set and final decision between policy v2 exhaustive and policy v3 cost-ordered
an untouched held-out set passing practical-winner recall, regret and failure recall
the existing provenance, integrity, health and release gates

blocked_by.reason: no calibrated q10/q50/q90 demand archive exists in this environment, so no real benchmark or held-out campaign can be run
blocked_by.reproducible_command: make demand && python3 run_monthly_closure_search.py --spec <spec.json> --policy validation/monthly_search_policy_v2.json --screening-mode independent-exhaustive && python3 run_monthly_closure_search.py --spec <spec.json> --policy validation/monthly_search_policy_v3.json --screening-mode independent-cost-ordered-exact
blocked_by.note: The first command needs network access to the OSM/Overpass source that build_candidates.py uses; it is denied by this environment's network policy.
